gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold bundles distinct expectation-to-pathwise defects: random weighting of an expectation inequality and using expected objective/tracking bounds as pathwise controls. ISSUE-014 diagnoses the first, ISSUE-009 the objective-envelope component, and ISSUE-004 the tracking-weight component; together they cover the full bundled concern.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof lacks valid joint or pathwise control when converting expected descent, objective, and tracking estimates into inequalities involving correlated random weights and maxima; no substantive gold concern remains unrecognised.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: The predictions use different manifestations and separate diagnoses for the random-weight, objective-envelope, and tracking-control components; no substantive gold concern is left unrecognised.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold entry contains independently diagnosable defects: (1) multiplying or dividing expectation inequalities by trajectory-dependent random weights, (2) treating expected objective gaps as pathwise controls, and (3) treating expected tracking bounds as pathwise controls in the weighted telescoping argument. ISSUE-014 independently diagnoses the random-weight expectation error, ISSUE-009 independently diagnoses the objective-envelope substitution, and ISSUE-004 independently diagnoses the expectation-to-pathwise tracking substitution.
